brief:
Merge allowance: merge when /ship's merge gate is clean, nothing wider.
Standing waivers, the only holds you may pass without stopping:
  1. Codex answers a review request with a usage-limit notice: drive the fallback reviewer and record Codex as not landed; do not hold the merge gate for it.
  2. A live end-to-end proof needs a real T3 server or other machines: prove it through the scripts over fake CLIs and say so in the PR body.
Any hold outside the merge allowance and these waivers stops at the gate: end with the gate state and the hold named, and do not work around it; the super agent escalates it to the owner.
A ruling from the super agent or the owner arrives in your thread: act on it, and never write it into a PR body (the body records what you did and checked).
Commands harmless to run (reads, tests, the repo's own checks) need no hold.
Other runs share this machine: stop only the processes you started, by their PID (never `pkill` or `pgrep` by name or pattern), and run the heavy check (the full suite, a container) under a per-repo lock and a memory cap: `flock /tmp/super-agent-acme-widgets.lock systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=<G>G -p MemorySwapMax=0 <command>`.
Calls the owner allowed, no hold needed:
  Run `git push to the branch` without a hold: the owner allowed it on 2026-11-15.
Owner rulings:
  2026-11-15: Everywhere ruling.
  2026-11-15: Widgets on box ruling.
Lines for this repo and machine:
  Widgets fleet line.
  Box fleet line.
Note for this ticket:
  Check the migration first.
A turn that ends only to wait on your own background work (a check, a CI wait, a subagent) ends with this line, word for word, as its last line: `Waiting on my own background work.` The watcher reads it as still working and wakes the super agent for no stall until the stall window has passed. Your final message is the PR URL and the gate state below, never this line.
Work in the worktree you start in, on the branch it holds, and make no other: the PR is found by that branch.
End your last message with the PR URL and the gate state.
